editorial_contributions.text:
Summary: A fall coloring of a graph \(G\) is a proper coloring of the vertex set of \(G\) such that every vertex of \(G\) is a color dominating vertex in \(G\) (that is, it has at least one neighbor in each of the other color classes). The fall coloring number \(\chi_f(G)\) of \(G\) is the minimum size of a fall color partition of \(G\) (when it exists). Trivially, for any graph \(G\), \(\chi(G)\leq \chi_f(G)\).

 In this paper, we show the existence of an infinite family of graphs \(G\) with prescribed values for \(\chi(G)\) and \(\chi_f(G)\). We also obtain the smallest non-fall colorable graphs with a given minimum degree \(\delta\) and determine their number. These answer two of the questions raised by \textit{J. E. Dunbar}, \textit{S. M. Hedetniemi}, {ıtS. T. Hedetniemi}, \textit{D. P. Jacobs}, \textit{J. Knisely}, \textit{R. C. Laskar} and \textit{D. F. Rall} [J. Comb. Math. Comb. Comput. 33, 257--273 (2000; Zbl 0962.05020)].

editorial_contributions.text:
The chromatic number of a graph \(G\) is written \(\chi(G)\). A proper \(k\)-coloring of a graph \(G\) with color classes \(V_1, \dots, V_k\) is a {\parindent=6mm \begin{itemize}\item[-] \(k\)-fall coloring if each vertex in \(V_i\) is adjacent to at least one vertex in \(V_j\), \(j\not= i\); the last, respectively, largest positive integer \(k\) for which \(G\) has a \(k\)-fall coloring is denoted by \(\chi_f(G)\), respectively, \(\Psi_f(G)\); \item[-] \(b\)-coloring if each \(V_i\) has a vertex adjacent to at least one vertex in \(V_j\), \(j\not= i\); the largest positive integer \(k\) for which \(G\) has a \(b\)-coloring using \(k\) colors is denoted by \(\phi(G)\); \item[-] partial Grundy coloring if, for each \(2\leq i\leq k\), there exists a vertex in \(V_i\) that is adjacent to at least one vertex in each \(V_j\), \(j < i\); the largest positive integer \(k\) for which \(G\) has a partial Grundy coloring with \(k\) colors is denoted by \(\partial\Gamma(G)\); \item[-] complete coloring if the union of two color classes is not an independent set of \(G\); the largest positive integer \(k\) for which \(G\) has a complete coloring with \(k\) colors is denoted by \(\Psi(G)\). 

\end{itemize}} It is clear that for any graph \(G\) admitting a fall coloring, \(\chi(G)\leq \chi_f(G)\leq \Psi_f(G)\leq \phi(G)\leq \partial\Gamma(G)\leq \Psi(G)\). The authors exhibit an infinite family of graphs \(G\) with a strictly increasing color chain: \(\chi(G)< \chi_f(G)< \Psi_f(G)< \phi(G)< \partial\Gamma(G)< \Psi(G)\). The existence of such a chain was raised in [\textit{J.E. Dunbar}, \textit{S.M. Hedetniemi}, \textit{S.T. Hedetniemi}, \textit{D.P. Jacobs}, \textit{J. Kniseley}, \textit{R.C. Laskar}, and \textit{D.F. Rall}, ``Fall coloring of graphs,'' J. Comb. Math. Comb. Comput. 33, 257--273 (2000); Zbl 0962.05020)]

editorial_contributions.text:
Let \(G\) be a finite and simple graph, with \(n=|V(G)|\), and let \(\chi(G)\) be its chromatic number, which is the smallest integer \(k\) for which \(G\) admits a \(k\)-colouring. The reconfiguration graph of the \(k\)-colourings, denoted by \(\mathcal R_k(G)\), is the graph whose vertices are the \(k\)-colourings of \(G\) and two vertices in \(\mathcal R_k(G)\) are adjacent if the colourings they correspond to differ in colour on exactly one vertex. \(G\) is said to be \(k\)-mixing if \(\mathcal R_k(G)\) is connected, and recolourable if \(G\) is \(k\)-mixing for all \(k>\chi(G)\). The \(k\)-recolouring diameter of \(G\) is the diameter of \(\mathcal R_k(G)\). A \(k\)-colouring of a graph \(G\) is called frozen if it is an isolated vertex in \(\mathcal R_k(G)\) (in the literature, frozen colourings have also been called fall colouring, and the term indominable graph has been used for a graph admitting a frozen colouring).

For a fixed graph \(H\), a graph \(G\) is called \(H\)-free if no induced subgraph of \(G\) is isomorphic to \(H\). In this paper the authors consider frozen colourings of \(2K_2\)-free graphs and recolourable \(2K_2\)-free graphs, by proving the following theorems:

Theorem 1. For every \(k\ge 4\), there is a \(k\)-chromatic \(2K_2\)-free graph with a frozen \((k+1)\)-colouring.

Theorem 2. Every \(3\)-chromatic \(2K_2\)-free graph \(G\) is recolourable with \(l\)-recolouring diameter at most \(14n\), for all \(l\ge \chi(G)+1\).

To prove Theorem 1, the authors give several infinite classes of \(2K_2\)-free graphs with frozen colourings and provide an operation, which requires some restrictions on the graph, that transforms a \(k\)-chromatic graph with a frozen \((k+1)\)-colouring into a \((k+1)\)-chromatic graph with a frozen \((k+2)\)-colouring and that preserves being \(2K_2\)-free.
